newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Privredna Banka says to increase loans.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Privredna Banka says to increase loans.

text.p: Croatia's largest bank and prime candidate for rehabilitation, Privredna Banka, said on Tuesday it would increase loans to clients on the back of a 7.3 percent rise in deposits to the end of September.

Advisor Alma Krajina said total deposits rose to 1.2 billion German marks and term-term savings were up strongly, allowing the bank to earmark another 36 million marks for long-term credits this year on top of an original 69 million.
She told a news conference the bank had so far placed 83 percent of this amount, primarily to citizens and private entrepreneurs.
Although still low at 8.3 percent, the share of citizens' kuna deposits increased from 6.4 percent at the beginning of the year while the rest was accounted for by hard currency.
"This is a good sign of regained confidence in the domestic currency," Krajina said.
The new deposits in foreign exchange, rising steadily since Croatia broke away from former Yugoslavia five years ago, were up 15.3 percent in the first nine months this year.
They now represent some 75 percent of the total with the rest accounted for by blocked pre-1991 foreign exchange liabilities, which are part of the public debt.

Following a decline in interbank rates to under 10 percent and lower mandatory reserves, the bank shaved its rates again at the beginning of September after first cutting them in June and scrapping the interest on sight deposits and giro accounts.

Its lending rates now range from 9.5 percent on loans to citizens for the purchase of property and 10.5 percent for prime company borrowers to 15 percent to other clients. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
